rules_summary.title: lairs_and_encounters_monster_stats_and_training_rules
rules_summary.source_note: Summarized from the uploaded section. Example stat-blocks and illustrative examples are omitted unless they add unique mechanics.

default_scores.rule: Most monsters are assumed to have 9 in all ability scores unless assigned otherwise.

general_rules.rule: Monster ability scores are measured relative to their own species, not to the human average.
Scores less than 9 or greater than 12 apply bonuses or penalties to related rolls and throws, using normal character modifiers except where this section overrides them.

strength.rule: Adjust attack throws and damage rolls for natural attacks by cross-referencing Strength score against the average damage of each natural attack.

load_rule.humanoid: adjust maximum load by strength_modifier × (normal_load ÷ 5), rounded to nearest stone
load_rule.rounding: round 0.5 up if negative, down if positive

intelligence.rule: Sapient monsters gain bonus proficiencies and languages from Intelligence as characters do.
Sapient monsters that cast arcane spells increase spells in repertoire at each spell level by their Intelligence bonus.
Animals, vermin, and fantastic creatures of animal intelligence do not gain proficiencies, languages, or spells from Intelligence.
For creatures of animal intelligence, Intelligence determines trainability: maximum tricks known equals 5 plus Intelligence modifier.

If a creature of animal intelligence has Intelligence modifier plus trainability modifier of 5 or more, the Judge may treat it as semi-sapient and capable of primitive communication, simple math, and basic tool use.
Mindless monsters, including most constructs except gargoyles and all oozes, have no Intelligence score or trainability modifier.

dexterity.rule: For non-humanoid monsters, encounter movement adjustment equals 10' × Dexterity bonus × (movement_rate ÷ 120').
Combat movement adjustment equals one-third of encounter movement adjustment.
Wilderness movement adjustment equals the lower of Dexterity bonus or Constitution bonus × 2 miles × (movement_rate ÷ 120').

constitution.rule: For living monsters, Constitution represents health and vitality; for constructs, sturdiness; for undead, negative animus.
Add Constitution bonus or penalty to each Hit Die roll.
Hit Dice gained beyond the maximum normally permitted for the monster’s size do not receive Constitution bonus.

charisma.rule: Add Charisma bonus or penalty to the monster’s morale and to the morale of monsters it leads.
Mindless monsters do not have Charisma scores.

proficiencies_for_monsters.rule: Most sapient monsters have proficiencies, but routine non-adventuring proficiencies can usually be ignored unless the monster is notably intelligent, dangerous, or trained.

starting_proficiencies.rule: Each sapient monster begins with Monster proficiency, one class proficiency, and one general proficiency.
starting_proficiencies.monster_proficiency_definition: The Monster proficiency covers the creature’s species-appropriate survival and everyday capabilities, serving as the monster equivalent of Adventuring.

additional_proficiencies.rule: Gain additional general proficiencies equal to Intelligence bonus.
If the monster has more Hit Dice than normal for its species, treat each extra Hit Die as a fighter level for gaining additional class and general proficiencies.
Gain one additional general proficiency when reaching middle-aged, old, and ancient age categories.

transformed_monsters.rule: If a sapient monster is transformed into another creature type with different or absent age categories, it continues gaining age-based proficiencies according to its original age categories.
Once it reaches its original ancient age category, it no longer gains proficiencies from age even if it survives indefinitely.

ageless_monsters.rule: Creatures lacking some or all age categories gain fewer or no age-based proficiencies.
Elves remain adult until death and therefore do not gain proficiencies for old or ancient categories.

recruitment.rule: Characters with Beast Friendship or Friends of Birds and Beasts can recruit animals, including giant and prehistoric animals, as henchmen.
All adventurers can recruit sapient beastmen, giants, humanoids, fantastic creatures, and undead as henchmen.
Monstrous henchmen count against normal henchman limits.
Normal animals may be bought in markets; some sapient monsters may be hired in large towns and cities; otherwise monstrous henchmen are recruited from encounters.
A monster must have fewer Hit Dice than its employer has levels. Monsters of 14 HD or more can only be recruited by more powerful monsters.
Employment can be offered at the start of an encounter only if the monster’s reaction is Neutral, Indifferent, or Friendly, or after combat if it is defeated and captured.
The adventurer must be able to communicate intelligibly with the monster.

Use a 2d6 reaction roll to determine response to an employment offer. Use the normal reaction-to-hiring table for market or peaceful encounters; use the Irrefusable Offer table for defeated and captured monsters.
Apply the adventurer’s Charisma modifier and any Diplomacy, Intimidation, or similar bonuses to the recruitment roll.
Apply a -2 penalty if adventurer and monster have opposite alignments.
If the monster is independent, apply its morale modifier as a penalty to recruitment. If it belonged to a defeated group, apply its prior leader’s morale modifier instead.
The Judge may apply other situational modifiers.

row.effect: Pretends to accept in order to betray the employer when possible; actively works against the employer’s interests.
Pretends to accept to save its life; deserts when safe opportunity appears, possibly harming the employer during escape.
Accepts with uncertain loyalties; begins with morale -2 instead of 0.

payment.rule: Sapient monstrous henchmen typically receive at least 15% of the employer’s income plus a monthly fee for food, lodging, and expenses.
Determine monthly fee using the normal henchman monthly fee table, substituting Hit Dice for level.
Animal henchmen do not require a share of income, but their upkeep equals supply cost plus additional wages equal to a henchman of the same Hit Dice.

advancement.rule: To advance from 1 HD to 2 HD, a monstrous henchman requires 3,000 XP plus 500 XP per special ability (*).
The XP requirement doubles with each additional Hit Die; round values greater than 20,000 XP to the nearest 1,000.
Sapient monsters may exceed their size-based maximum by up to 5 additional Hit Dice, gaining a fixed 2 hp per extra Hit Die and no Constitution bonus.
Enchanted creatures and undead may advance in Hit Dice without limit.

improvements_per_hit_die.rule: Attack throws, hit points, and saving throws improve by 1 per Hit Die gained.
Armor Class improves by 1 per 2 Hit Dice, to a maximum improvement equal to the monster’s own starting Hit Dice.
Average damage increases by 2 hp total, divided among attacks as the Judge decides.
Sapient monsters may gain proficiencies as fighters when advancing; monsters of animal intelligence gain one additional trainable trick.

noncombatant_monsters.rule: Species may distinguish combatants from noncombatants because of sexual dimorphism, unequal combat training, or both.
Noncombatants usually have 25% to 75% of the Hit Dice and average hit points of combatants of the same species.
Noncombatant Armor Class, damage, and morale are usually adjusted to match a similar creature of reduced Hit Dice.
Noncombatants with fewer than 1/4 HD have 1 hp and do not fight at all.

young_and_old_monsters.rule: Unless the monster listing states otherwise, young and aged monsters use the Monster Age Adjustment and Monster Age Damage Calculator tables.
Baby monsters are two size categories smaller than adults; child monsters are one size category smaller; adolescent and older monsters are full size.
For Hit Dice calculations, treat each printed +1 or -1 as ±0.25 HD; round to the nearest 0.25 and convert back to + or - notation.
Creatures reduced below 1/4 HD have 1 hp and do not fight.
For movement adjustment, multiply the table’s movement adjustment by movement_rate ÷ 120' and round to nearest 5'.
For maximum load adjustment, round to nearest stone; round 0.5 up if negative, down if positive.
For damage adjustment, cross-reference the original attack damage against the Monster Age Damage Calculator.

table.name: monster_age_adjustment_and_damage_calculator
table.note: * Movement adjustment is per 120' of encounter movement and applies to non-humanoid monsters only.

aging_for_monsters_with_ability_scores.rule: If using monster ability scores, age effects for AC, movement, Hit Dice, and damage can be calculated by applying ability penalties instead of the age table: -6 for baby/ancient, -4 for child/old, and -2 for adolescent/middle-aged.
Size and maximum load adjustments still use the Monster Age Adjustment table.
The Judge may use either method when the results differ.

noncombatant_monsters_and_experience_poi.rule: A noncombatant monster of 1 HD or less requires 100 XP plus 15 XP per hit point bonus or special ability (*) to become a combatant.
The XP requirement doubles with each HD; round values over 20,000 XP to the nearest 1,000.
Upon becoming a combatant, the monster immediately gains +1 hit point per full Hit Die; each 4 hit points gained this way equals 1 Hit Die.
After becoming a combatant, it may gain Hit Dice or levels normally.

overview.rule: Taming teaches a monster to submit to handling without threatening or injuring its handler and companions.
Training teaches one or more tricks.
Animal trainers perform taming and training.
Animals, vermin, and fantastic creatures of animal intelligence must be tamed before training.
Fantastic creatures of sapient intelligence, giants, and humanoids cannot be tamed, but may voluntarily accept training.
Sapient creatures generally only need training when serving as mounts or war mounts.
Constructs, enchanted creatures, oozes, and undead can neither be tamed nor trained.
Initial taming requires one training period. Teaching the first trick requires one additional training period. Each later trick requires one-half training period.
Sapient monsters that voluntarily accept training skip taming and may proceed directly to tricks.
Training period assumes training begins when the creature is a baby or child.
If training starts when the creature is an adolescent or adult, taming time is multiplied by 6 and each trick’s training time is multiplied by 2.
Maximum tricks known is normally 2d4, or 5 plus/minus Intelligence modifier when the optional monster ability score rules are used, modified further by trainability modifier where applicable.
The trainer learns the creature’s trick limit when it is tamed.

animal_trainers.rule: Each rank in Animal Training covers one creature type.
Creatures sharing a Monster Listings entry are generally the same type, except dire, giant, and prehistoric animals, which count as separate types.
To train multiple creature types, take Animal Training multiple times.
To train dire, giant, prehistoric animals, or fantastic creatures, first take Animal Training for a similar normal animal type.
If a creature is gigantic size or larger, handlers cost at least 150 gp per month.
To train mounts for combat, the trainer must also be a marshal of the appropriate type and earns whichever wage is higher.
Light cavalry marshals generally earn 60 gp per month; heavy cavalry marshals generally earn 120 gp per month.
A single trainer can train and manage up to six monsters at once.
Monster whispering means one trainer works one-on-one with one monster for the entire training period; this increases maximum tricks by 2.
Adult flying creatures can only be trained by monster whispering.

tricks.trick: Attack apparent enemies; the handler may designate a particular target.
Allow the handler to ride on its back.
Come to the handler even when it otherwise would not.
Defend the handler or another designated character, even without a fresh command when a threat is present.
Break off combat or otherwise back down. Without this trick the creature keeps fighting until forced to flee or until its opponent is defeated.
Retrieve an indicated item, or a random object if none is designated.
Stay in place and prevent others from approaching.
Follow the handler closely even into places it normally would not go.
Search an area for anything obviously alive or animate.
Remain in place until the handler returns; do not challenge passersby, but still defend itself if needed.
Carry, pull, or push more than normal load.
tricks.rule: A trained monster obeys its trainer and any additional handlers the trainer introduces to it.
Handlers need not have the matching Animal Training proficiency, but without it they can safely control only one monster at a time unless role rules say otherwise.

role.name: drover
role.summary: Brings livestock together and moves the herd.

role.name: guard
role.summary: Attacks designated targets and defends designated characters or locations; accompanies handlers when requested and remains loyally in place when handlers are absent.
role.note: Creatures lacking the right intelligence or temperament are usually trained as hunters instead.

role.name: hunter
role.summary: Accompanies handlers on hunts, tracks and kills designated targets.

role.name: livestock
role.summary: Is easily herded; does not accept riders, pull loads, or carry burdens.

handling.proficient: any number if same social group and proficient or under drover control

role.note: Domesticated herd animals can serve as livestock without taming or training.

role.name: mount
role.summary: Carries a rider and accepts directions; no barding; no melee charges except against natural predators; does not attack with natural weapons while carrying a rider.

handling.proficient: outside battle: up to 6 mounts if proficient, one ridden and others ponied; in battle: ridden mount only with Riding proficiency
handling.unproficient: lead one safely; riding without proficiency requires save vs Paralysis each round or fall

role.note: Sapient riding creatures must also be trained as mounts.

role.name: war_mount
role.morale_change: +2 morale, maximum +2, except sapient creatures do not gain this morale increase
role.summary: Carries a rider into battle, accepts barding, charges into melee, and attacks the rider’s target with natural weapons.
role.note: An unridden war mount functions as a guard creature.

role.name: workbeast
role.summary: Pulls heavy loads or carries burdens; does not accept a rider.
role.note: In stress or battle reacts according to natural instincts.

magic_and_monster_training.rule: Ordinary animals within 5 miles of an elven fastness are always considered tame for training by resident elves.

Animal henchmen recruited by this power are automatically tame toward the character, can be monster-whisperer trained for any role their trick limit allows, do not require separate Animal Training for that character, and the character always counts as proficient when handling them.

A charmed creature is immediately considered tame for training by the spellcaster. Appropriate Animal Training is still required. Training proceeds at child rates even if the creature is older. If the charm ends, the creature becomes wild again until re-charmed.

The character always counts as proficient when handling trained animals in their roles. A friendly untrained animal may be handled as if trained for any role it can fulfill, though the character is not treated as actually proficient unless he has the relevant proficiency. The character automatically counts as monster whispering when training animals he can speak with.

encounters_with_tamed_monsters.rule: If a tame trained monster is uncontrolled, make a reaction roll when a character approaches it.
Apply +2 if the approaching character has the appropriate Animal Training proficiency.
Characters with Beast Friendship or under Speak with Animals count as proficient for this purpose.
On a reaction roll of 9 or higher, the character immediately becomes the animal’s handler.

taming_and_training_by_race.rule: If a trainer has affinity with the monster, guard training counts as only two tricks.
If a trainer has no affinity, base training period is doubled for all purposes and morale of the trained monster is reduced by 2 while handled by that trainer.
Mounts refuse riders with no affinity; treat attempted riding anyway as unproficient riding.
War mounts accept no-affinity riders but function only as normal mounts for them.

definitions.rule: Adult weight in pounds. Adolescents weigh 75% of adult weight. Children weigh 25% to 75% of adult weight, averaging 50%. Babies weigh 5% to 25% of adult weight, averaging 15%. Eggs weigh 5% of adult weight.
Use size categories M, L, H, G, and C. If height and weight imply different categories, weight usually determines size.
Most creatures carry normal load at full movement and maximum load equal to twice normal load at half movement.
Humanoids may carry normal load at full movement, half again normal load at three-quarters movement, twice normal load at half movement, and four times normal load at one-quarter movement.
Role codes are D, G, H, L, M, WM, and WB. Training is N/A for sapient creatures unless typically used as mounts.

Market price for a tamed and trained adolescent or adult. Animals and creatures of animal intelligence may be sold as property in most realms. Sapient creatures may only be sold as slaves in Chaotic realms permitting slavery; otherwise they must be hired as mercenaries.
Each ability score of 13-15 adds 25% to cost. Each ability score of 16-17 adds 100%. Each ability score of 18 adds 400%.
Reduce price by 15% for each score of 3, by 10% for each score of 4-5, and by 5% for each score of 6-8.
Format is Baby/Child/Adolescent/Adult/Middle Aged/Old/Ancient/Maximum. Oviparous creatures use E instead of 0 to indicate beginning life as an egg.

These values are for untamed, untrained creatures. Adolescents are priced as adults. Eggs are priced as babies. A dash means the age category is essentially worthless and usually unavailable for sale.
Each dragon age category is purchased as an adult creature; there is no separate baby form within a later dragon age category.
Cost per week to maintain an adult creature. Eggs, herbivores grazing on a pasture, and carnivores hunting on a range require no supplied provisions.
For baby, child, and adolescent creatures, multiply adult supply cost by the creature’s age as a fraction of age at adulthood, rounding to nearest 0.5 gp.
Months required to tame a creature or teach its first trick. Dash means the creature cannot be trained.

Modifier to maximum tricks. S means sapient and not limited to a trick count, though sapient creatures still need mount or war mount training when serving in those roles. Dash means the creature cannot be trained.

uncertainties.item: The Monster Age Damage Calculator header is visually compressed in the DOCX extraction. The age rows and adjusted results are preserved, and the source-average-damage bands include one inferred band of 6.5 to keep the 17-column structure consistent with the extracted rows.

Several role-code cells in the characteristics tables appear corrupted in the source extraction: Cat, Saber-Tooth, Riding has role code "W"; Stegosaurus, Riding, Triceratops, Riding, and T. Rex, Riding have role code "R". The printed role code was preserved exactly rather than normalized.
Bugbear, Dire has a blank baby_value cell in the DOCX extraction. The blank is preserved.
Faerie, Sprite has a blank normal_load cell in the DOCX extraction. The blank is preserved.
